Matt Coler received his PhD from the Free University of Amsterdam in 2010. After a postdoctoral appointment at his alma mater, he joined an AI start-up focused on acoustic sensors, where he headed the cognitive systems unit from 2012 to 2016. In 2016 he returned to academia full-time at the University of Groningen. He is currently an Associate Professor of Speech Technology at Campus Fryslân, University of Groningen, where he directs the MSc Speech Technology program and heads the Governance & Technology Department.

## Funding

Roles in international research projects with combined budgets over €15M, funded by EU, national, and regional programmes, in speech technology and AI, minority and low-resource languages, language preservation, human-centred technology, and acoustic sensing. Small grants for feasibility studies and virtual exchange are not listed.

- **2017–2025**: **H2020-MSCA-RISE-2017: COLING**, *Minority Languages, Major Opportunities: Collaborative Research, Community Engagement and Innovative Educational Tools*. €1.58M total (€189k for my team). Steering Committee Member and Work Package Leader. Established an international research exchange with the Smithsonian Institution.
- **2016–2019**: **H2020-FET-Open: Phoenix**, *Exploring the Unknown through Reincarnation and Co-evolution*. Evolving hardware technologies for extreme environments. €3.6M total (€237k for my team). Work Package Leader and Management Team Member.
- **2016–2019**: **Polish Science Foundation TEAM Grant**, *Language as a cure: linguistic vitality as a tool for psychological well-being, health and economic sustainability*. €814k.
- **2015–2018**: **Interreg VA ID3AS**, *Acoustic event detection*. €9.75M total (€200k for my team).
